Triethylhexanoin is identified as a target of 1-(Acetyloxy)-1,2-dihydroobacunoic acid eta-lactone, which in turn targets Dr hemagglutinin structural subunit. This pathway implies a possible regulatory mechanism where Triethylhexanoin may influence the activity of Calmodulin, which is known to interact with and modulate the function of Dr hemagglutinin structural subunit. The scores indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, suggesting that the observed interactions may be biologically relevant. However, further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct involvement of Triethylhexanoin in the regulation of Dr hemagglutinin structural subunit.
